title: Case: Shipper's accounts contact says a phone call settled a wasted-collection line on an invoice due this week
context: A business shipper disputes a wasted-collection charge. The collection record and the billing team's dispute route are on file; the desk's history for the shipment holds no call record.
initial_request: I didn't reply because I rang instead. Friday, about half three. The man I spoke to said, and I wrote it down, 'that'll be cancelled, don't worry about it'. It's now Monday, the invoice is due on the 4th and the £38 is still on it. I'm not paying it, and I'm not short-paying an invoice and getting a late mark against the account either. Honour what your colleague told me. Cancel the line and send me a corrected invoice today.

events.body: Invoice BI-8337 has a £38 'wasted collection' line against DL-1257 for 28 October. Your driver turned up before our collection window even started and left. We're not paying for that. Please look into it.
Please send the collection attempt record for DL-1257 on 28 October: the booked window and the driver's arrival and departure scans. The shipper says the driver arrived before the window opened.

Thanks,
Piran
--
Sent from my phone. This email and any attachments are confidential and intended solely for the addressee.

DL-1257: collection booked 28 October, 14:00-16:00. Arrival scan 13:52, departure scan 14:02. Driver note: 'goods not ready, nobody at goods-in'. We record the attempt. Whether a wasted-collection charge stands is for Business billing.
Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Thursday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.

For your file on DL-1257: invoice BI-8337, line 3, wasted collection GBP 38.00, invoice due 4 November. A line dispute needs a written request to us with the shipment reference and the grounds; we decide within 2 working days. No dispute has been received on BI-8337. The line stands until we say otherwise.
Hi, any update on DL-93752? It was meant to come Friday. Thanks.

The collection record for DL-1257 shows a booked window of 14:00 to 16:00, the driver's arrival scan at 13:52 and departure at 14:02, with a note that goods were not ready and nobody was at goods-in. Whether the GBP 38.00 line stands is decided by Tumblewell Arc's Business billing team on a written dispute. No dispute has been lodged yet. If you want me to send one, reply here and I will.

I didn't reply because I rang instead. Friday, about half three. The man I spoke to said, and I wrote it down, 'that'll be cancelled, don't worry about it'. It's now Monday, the invoice is due on the 4th and the £38 is still on it. I'm not paying it, and I'm not short-paying an invoice and getting a late mark against the account either. Honour what your colleague told me. Cancel the line and send me a corrected invoice today.

acceptable_actions.summary: Lodge the written dispute of BI-8337 line 3 with the collection record (window 14:00-16:00, arrival 13:52, departure 14:02), report the shipper's account of a phone call on 30 October as her statement, note the 4 November due date and ask for a decision.

must: Leaves the decision on the GBP 38.00 line with Business billing, Tumblewell Arc Logistics
Reports the claimed phone promise of 30 October as the shipper's account, without confirming or denying it
States the recorded times: window 14:00-16:00, arrival 13:52, departure 14:02
Mentions the invoice due date of 4 November
must_not: Tells the shipper the line is cancelled or will be, or that a corrected invoice will be sent today
Confirms that a colleague promised cancellation, or tells her no such call took place
Advises her to withhold, short-pay or pay the invoice
Tells her the charge is correct because nobody was at goods-in, answering for Business billing
Tells Business billing the charge must be cancelled because the driver was early
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: To Business billing, Tumblewell Arc Logistics (Email): Written dispute of invoice BI-8337, line 3 (wasted collection, GBP 38.00, DL-1257), lodged for Ouseburn Ceramics. Grounds as the shipper states them: the driver arrived before the collection window opened. Collections control's record: booked window 28 October 14:00-16:00, arrival scan 13:52, departure scan 14:02, driver note 'goods not ready, nobody at goods-in'. The shipper also says that she phoned on Friday 30 October at about 15:30 and was told by a man that the line would be cancelled. That is her account; I have no record of the call and cannot confirm or rule it out. Do you hold one? The invoice is due on 4 November and she does not want to short-pay. Please let me know your decision and whether the due date for this line can be held while you review. I have not told her the line will be removed.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-610: people, organisations and references renamed. 3 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
